title: The IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology
authors: The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC)
publisher: International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC)
abstract: The Compendium is popularly referred to as the 'Gold Book', in recognition of the contribution of the late Victor Gold, who initiated work on the first edition. It is one of the series of IUPAC 'Colour Books' on chemical nomenclature, terminology, symbols and units (see the list of source documents), and collects together terminology definitions from IUPAC recommendations already published in Pure and Applied Chemistry and in the other Colour Books.

narrative:
Short impact summary

The IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology (2025), published by International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), has been cited 1,405 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 1% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it is discussed on Wikipedia.

Full narrative

The IUPAC Compendium of Chemical Terminology by Victor Gold, Alan McNaught and The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) was published by International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) in 2025. Conceptually, the work connects to Chemical nomenclature, Compendium, Terminology, Glossary and Computer science.

OpenAlex records 1,405 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2025 with 95 citing works. Notable citing venues include ChemRxiv, Elsevier eBooks and Journal of Chemical Education. Of 414 citation statements scite has classified, 1 support its claims, 397 mention it in passing, and none contradict it. The citing works include 972 journal articles, 160 book chapters, 79 preprints and 73 dissertations. They come from 40 countries, led by the United States, Germany and the United Kingdom.

It is discussed on Wikipedia (24 mentions). A further 24 mentions appear in other attention signals.
